papers.title: Structures preserved by primitive actions of $S_\omega$
papers.abstract: We present a dichotomy for structures $A$ that are preserved by primitive actions of $S_{\omega} = \text{Sym}({\mathbb N})$: such a structure primitively positively constructs all finite structures and the constraint satisfaction problem is NP-complete, or the constraint satisfaction problem for $A$ is in P. To prove our result, we study the first-order reducts of the Johnson graph $J(k)$, for $k \geq 2$, whose automorphism group $G$ equals the action of $\text{Sym}({\mathbb N})$ on the set $V$ of $k$-element subsets of $\mathbb N$. We use the fact that $J(k)$ has a finitely bounded homogeneous Ramsey expansion and that $G$ is a maximal closed subgroup of $\text{Sym}(V)$.

papers.title: Proofs Without Nominals: G\"odel's Ontological Argument, its Shallow Embedding, and the Open Questions of the Monatshefte Notes
papers.abstract: The shallow embedding of higher-order modal logic in classical higher-order logic, used in Benzm\"uller and Scott's Notes on G\"odel's and Scott's variants of the ontological argument, reaches beyond the modal object language: its quantifiers range over domains containing the nominals and satisfaction operators of hybrid logic. A proof using one proves a theorem of the embedding, not necessarily of the modal logic. Whether a result is one of the modal logic can be settled by replaying it in an explicit calculus, or, more cheaply and for all results at once, by analysing what the embedding's proofs substitute. Every statement the Notes prove has a proof in the embedding substituting nothing outside the object language, 294 of them explicit. The Notes' own proofs substitute none either; what it flags are terms a prover introduced. A soundness theorem over general models closed under the object language, and a sentence of that language the embedding proves but which fails in such a model, fix what the certificate says. The Notes' three open questions are settled too, without nominals, but by the empty instance of the conjunction axiom, too cheaply to convince. Generalised to G\"odel's "any number of summands", the axiom covers the empty conjunction and the singleton. This article restricts it to at least two different conjuncts, a non-degenerate reading of G\"odel's footnote, and settles them again without nominals. In effect only the empty conjunction is excluded; the singleton comes back with the other axioms. In one variant the restriction refutes the possible existence of a God-like being; the answers return, with no side condition, once the Notes' non-emptiness clause is confined to G\"odel's essence. Every theorem here is verified in Isabelle/HOL and independently in Lean 4, the separating model in its propositional part; the countermodels are Nitpick's, checked by the build.

papers.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic with Program Costs
papers.abstract: We introduce $\mathbb{N}\mathtt{PDL}$, a resource-aware variant of Propositional Dynamic Logic ($\mathtt{PDL}$) capable of accounting for program costs measured by natural numbers (such as time or space in the sense of computability theory). In this framework, programs correspond to transition systems weighted by extended natural numbers, and the syntax of our logic includes formulas expressing which properties are reachable by program executions within specific cost constraints. First, we explain how the standard program constructs of non-deterministic choice, sequential composition, iteration, and tests are interpreted in this weighted setting and establish the validity of their corresponding reduction axioms. Using an appropriate adaptation of the (Fischer-Ladner) filtration technique, we proceed to prove decidability and completeness for $\mathbb{N}\mathtt{PDL}$ as our main results. We furthermore provide upper and lower complexity bounds for this logic using translations between standard $\mathtt{PDL}$ and $\mathbb{N}\mathtt{PDL}$.

papers.title: Coinduction in Grounded Arithmetic
papers.abstract: A grounded arithmetic counts a sentence as true only when a terminating process establishes it; a sentence no such process settles has no value. Such a logic can state that an event happens, but not that it never happens under unbounded choice. This paper extends such a logic so that it can. The base is Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) with Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA)'s least-fixed-point reading and ground induction. It adds a separate greatest-fixed-point former $\nu$ with Park's coinduction rule, proves that one former cannot carry both ground induction and coinduction, and adds a dichotomy rule: the classical disjunction between a least-fixed-point atom and the greatest-fixed-point atom of its dual, under a derivable premise that the body's leaves are decided. The systems are sound for an explicit model reading every $\nu$-body at its greatest fixed point, hence consistent; they agree with the least model wherever it has a value and prove sentences it leaves without one. The dichotomy replaces the underivable hypothesis that an order is well-founded by the derivable one that its steps are decided; the change of model pays for the move. With ground induction the dichotomy derives the omniscience rule of the sibling arithmetic OGA, so the system has no semantics whose certificates for universals are its own proofs. The systems prove, as single sentences, that every decided tree is well-founded or has an infinite branch given by a term, total in the new model; that random assignment terminates while its divergent twin runs forever; that a fair loop terminates and the alternating-bit protocol delivers every message; that open games are determined; that the termination gap in Nakata and Uustalu's trace semantics closes; and that Cinderella wins the bucket game at capacity three. Isabelle/HOL checks every result.

papers.title: Order-Invariant CFO Contains Local-Order-Invariant FO
papers.abstract: Order-invariant cluster first-order logic (CFO) and local-order-invariant first-order logic are two fragments of order-invariant first-order logic, both motivated by the study of invariant logics on classes of bounded degree. Our main result is that order-invariant CFO contains local-order-invariant FO on arbitrary classes of finite structures, settling the conjecture of Ghasemi and Grange that order-invariant CFO contains plain FO. By combining this with a collapse result of Ghasemi and Grange, we obtain the equivalence of FO, local-order-invariant FO, and order-invariant CFO on classes of finite colored graphs of bounded degree. The proof makes use of Gaifman normal form, which allows our translation from local-order-invariant FO to order-invariant CFO to be effective. Combined with the fixed-parameter tractability of model-checking for order-invariant CFO on bounded-degree colored graph classes, this shows that model-checking for local-order-invariant FO on bounded-degree colored graph classes is fixed-parameter tractable. To generalize our collapse and model-checking results beyond colored graphs, we use a method based on first-order interpretations which also yields a collapse of order-invariant FO to FO when restricted to graph classes of bounded shrub-depth. Finally, we give an application to the database-motivated frozen-witness logic of Abiteboul, Simon, and Vianu by showing that local-order-invariant FO contains deterministic frozen-witness FO, and thus that deterministic frozen-witness FO collapses to FO on classes of finite structures of bounded degree.

papers.title: Monadic Second-Order Logic of Permutations
papers.abstract: Permutations can be viewed as pairs of linear orders, or more formally as models over a signature consisting of two binary relation symbols. This approach was adopted by Albert, Bouvel and F\'eray, who studied the expressibility of first-order logic in this setting. We focus our attention on monadic second-order logic. Our results go in two directions. First, we investigate the expressive power of monadic second-order logic. We exhibit natural properties of permutations that can be expressed in monadic second-order logic but not in first-order logic. Additionally, we show that the property of having a fixed point is inexpressible even in monadic second-order logic. Secondly, we focus on the complexity of monadic second-order model checking. We show that there is an algorithm deciding if a permutation $\pi$ satisfies a given monadic second-order sentence $\varphi$ in time $f(|\varphi|, \operatorname{tw}(\pi)) \cdot n$ for some computable function $f$ where $n = |\pi|$ and $\operatorname{tw}(\pi)$ is the tree-width of $\pi$. On the other hand, we prove that the problem remains hard even when we restrict the permutation $\pi$ to a fixed hereditary class $\mathcal{C}$ with mild assumptions on $\mathcal{C}$.

papers.title: Cartesian closedness of lax comma categories
papers.abstract: For a finitely complete category X, we prove that the lax comma category Cat//X is cartesian closed if and only if its free coproduct completion Fam(X) is cartesian closed. The proof uses a change-of-base theorem: postcomposition with a functor induces a left adjoint between lax comma categories precisely when that functor is a left multiadjoint. We describe the exponentials and derive examples from known results on family categories.

papers.title: A localized packing lemma for sets of bounded $\operatorname{VC}_2$-dimension
papers.abstract: In the setting of abelian groups, Haussler's packing lemma implies that any subset of bounded $\operatorname{VC}$-dimension can be approximated by one of a small number of representative translates. While this exact statement is provably false under the weaker hypothesis that $A$ has bounded $\operatorname{VC}_2$-dimension, we show that in $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ a similar statement does hold after localization to cosets of subspaces depending on the individual translates. More precisely, given $\epsilon>0$ and $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_p^n$ with $\operatorname{VC}_2(A)<k$, we show that there exist $r\leq \epsilon^{-O_{k,p}(1)}$ and $g_1,\ldots, g_r\in \mathbb{F}_p^n$ with the property that for every $x\in \mathbb{F}_p^n$, there is a partition $\mathcal{C}_x$ of $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ into cosets of (possibly distinct) subgroups, each of index at most $\exp(\epsilon^{-O_{k,p}(1)})$, and a subcollection $\Omega_x\subseteq \mathcal{C}_x$ whose union has size at least $(1-\epsilon)|\mathbb{F}_p^n|$, such that on each $C\in \Omega_x$, the translate $A-x$ looks like one of $A-g_1,\ldots, A-g_r$, in the sense that $|((A-x)\Delta (A-g_{i_{x,C}}))\cap C|<\epsilon|C|$ for some $1\leq i_{x,C}\leq r$. We also prove a second version of this result in which each partition $\mathcal{C}_x$ is the set of cosets of a single subgroup $H_x$ of quasipolynomial index but where the bound on $r$ is a quadruple exponential.

papers.title: On the growth of weak regular partitions in k-uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: This paper classifies hereditary properties of k-uniform hypergraphs according to bounds in the weak hypergraph regularity lemma first developed by Chung. Specifically, we prove the bounds must grow at a constant, polynomial, exponential, or tower rate. This generalizes work in the 3-uniform case by the second author.

papers.title: Extension of kappa-additive measures
papers.abstract: We establish an extension theorem for kappa-additive probability measures, where kappa is an arbitrary uncountable cardinal. Starting from a <kappa-algebra, we define an outer measure using coverings of cardinality at most kappa and characterise measurable sets by approximation in outer measure of symmetric differences. We prove that these sets form a kappa-algebra carrying a complete kappa-additive extension of the original measure. The extension is unique on the generated kappa-algebra, and its completion is the minimal domain admitting a complete kappa-additive extension. We also establish attainment of the covering infimum and show why the closure assumption on the initial algebra is essential. Examples include a strict extension of classical Lebesgue measure under the additional hypothesis add N = aleph_1 < cov N.

papers.title: Well begun is half done: the computation of Eulerian paths
papers.abstract: We characterize the uniform computational strength of finding one-way Eulerian paths in countable graphs. For both directed and undirected graphs, this problem is Weihrauch-equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}\times\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$, where $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ is the jump of closed choice on the natural numbers. This refines the proof-theoretical strength of the existence of an Eulerian path given by the reverse mathematics framework. The $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ component comes entirely from the difficulty of choosing a starting vertex: with a valid start prescribed, the problem is equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}$. We also study the problem $\mathsf{OrientEP}$ of orienting an undirected graph while preserving the existence of a one-way Eulerian path. We prove $\mathsf{lim}_2<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{OrientEP}<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{2}'\sqcap\mathsf{Sort}_2$ and $\mathsf{OrientEP}\not\le_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}$.

papers.title: Quasitoposes as elementary quotient completions
papers.abstract: We characterise when the elementary quotient completion of an elementary doctrine, introduced in previous work by the first and third authors, is a quasitopos. Since the elementary quotient completion generalises the notion of exact completion of a cartesian category with weak equalisers to the setting of elementary doctrines, as proposed by F.W. Lawvere, the characterisation established in this paper, generalises previous results on exact completions, which include A. Carboni and E. Vitale's characterisation in terms of projective objects, Carboni and G. Rosolini's characterisation of locally cartesian closed exact completions, as revised by J. Emmenegger, and M. Menni's characterisation of exact completions that are toposes.

papers.title: Polyteam logics for quantum contextuality
papers.abstract: We introduce logics of dependence and independence over polyteams (that is, databases with multiple relation schemes), in a similar way as in arXiv:1704.02158v3 [cs.LO]. On this basis, we develop a logical framework in which we can express (in formulas) relevant properties about the statistics of a repeated quantum experiment. In this framework, we formalize Bell's theorem, and the Kochen-Specker theorem as failure of logical entailments, as it was suggested in arXiv:2107.10817v3 [math.LO]. The key feature of polyteam logics in action here is their power to express both local and global properties, with respect to the set of possible measurements. The point of this is at least twofold. Firstly, as in arXiv:1102.0264v7 [quant-ph], it gives a high-level (information-theoretic) understanding of these physical phenomena, that is not intrinsic to the physical objects involved. Secondly, since logical entailment is often (partially) axiomatizable, this framework incites us to tackle the question of contextuality computationally. We also define semiring-weighted polyteams along with logics on them, and use them to recover the probabilistic versions of the contextuality theorems mentioned above.

papers.title: Modular proof analysis and cut elimination for the Reflection Calculi $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$
papers.abstract: The reflection calculus with one modality is denoted by $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and its quantified generalization is known as $\mathsf{QRC}_1$. These decidable calculi are of interest since they generate the strictly positive fragments of the (quantified) provability logic for theories like Peano Arithmetic and Heyting Arithmetic. We introduce analytic cut-free calculi ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ for $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The new calculi derive sequents of the form $A\Longrightarrow B$ with $A,B$ strictly positive formulas. In particular, the new calculi do not use (multi)sets nor nested sequents. For both ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ it is shown that the cut-rule is admissible. As a consequence, it is proven that the calculi are deductively equivalent to $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The cutfree systems are used to prove uniform interpolation for the two reflection calculi. In addition, ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ is used to give a syntactic proof of Dashkov's Theorem to the extent that $\mathsf{RC}_1$ is the strictly positive fragment of the provability logic ${\mathsf{GL}}$. The paper also introduces non-analytic calculi that are conceptually easier but proof-theoretically behave badly. It is shown that even those systems allow direct cut-elimination: the benefits of the strict positivity outweigh the draw-backs of a non-analytic calculus in these cases.

papers.title: Some variants of function domination
papers.abstract: We investigate whether classical recursion-theoretic notions defined by function domination remain unchanged when success is required only on sets of prescribed asymptotic density. We establish robustness for many such notions and uncover unexpected connections between familiar degree properties by comparing upper and lower density. In contrast, pdomination, as defined by Chong, Hoi, Stephan and Turetsky, is not robust under density weakenings. We also answer a question of Kjos-Hanssen and Nies by characterizing superhighness as domination with a threshold boundedly limit recursive in the oracle. As an application, we introduce supermaximal sets, a strengthening of maximality whose degrees are exactly the superhigh r.e. degrees.

papers.title: Effective Hausdorff dimension one is cofinal in the K-degrees
papers.abstract: Every K-degree has an upper bound of effective Hausdorff dimension one and Kurtz random sequences are cofinal in the K-degrees.

papers.title: $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ Proves the Collapse of the Intersection Principles Hierarchy
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the pairwise intersection principle ($2\mathrm{IP}$) implies, over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$, the existence of a Cohen $1$-generic real relative to every given set. Together with the known implications, this yields the equivalence over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ of the finite intersection principle (FIP), $2\mathrm{IP}$, and $1$-GEN. In fact, FIP is equivalent to $n\mathrm{IP}$ for every fixed $n\geq 2$. These results give affirmative answers to Questions~1 and~2 of Cholak, Downey, and Igusa, and to Question~9.10.26 of Dzhafarov and Mummert. The proof uses cumulative, nested supports satisfying a finite Helly property and a decoding argument based on a least selected label. Neither $\Sigma^0_2$ induction nor $\Sigma^0_2$ bounding is required.

papers.title: 1-Genericity Is Not Weihrauch Reducible to the Finite Intersection Principle
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the problem of producing a Cohen $1$-generic real relative to a given oracle is not Weihrauch reducible to the finite intersection principle (FIP). More strongly, no nontrivial computable FIP instance admits a single Turing functional that produces an absolute $1$-generic real from every enumeration of every maximal centered set of indices. The argument combines a $1$-generic real that computes no perfect tree all of whose paths are $1$-generic with local constancy and a parametrization of maximal centered sets. This answers Question~9.10.25 of Dzhafarov and Mummert.

papers.title: Omitting Types for Infinitary Real-Valued Logic: A Topological Perspective
papers.abstract: For countable vocabularies, we extend the omitting types theorem for countable fragments of infinitary logic to Keisler's general real-valued structures by proving that the space of Henkin types of each such fragment is \v{C}ech-complete. The structures interpret function symbols arbitrarily and predicate symbols by bounded real-valued functions, while each formula carries a bound of its own. This extends the setting of Eagle's theorem from metric structures with a prescribed master metric to general structures whose vocabulary prescribes the sorts and bounds of the symbols. Following Keisler and Miller's treatment of logic without equality, we build models from closed terms. Morley's Baire category method then gives every satisfiable theory on a countable fragment a model with countable sorts omitting any countable family of types whose closed-term instances have empty interior in the space of Henkin types satisfying the theory.

papers.title: No Borel upper bound for the $F_\sigma$ equivalence relations
papers.abstract: We prove that the family of coset relations of $F_\sigma$ real linear subspaces of Banach space $\ell_1$ has no common upper bound among Borel equivalence relations in the sense of Borel reducibility. These relations are indexed by a well-founded tree. Consequently, on a Polish space, a universal $\Sigma^0_\alpha$ equivalence relation exists exactly when $\alpha=1$, and a universal $\Pi^0_\alpha$ equivalence relation exists exactly when $\alpha=1$ or $2$. This strengthens the earlier nonexistence theorem for a universal $F_\sigma$ equivalence relation. This also answers a question of Kanovei and Lyubetsky about universal equivalence relations in Borel classes.

papers.title: The 1-2-3 Conjecture for Borel Combinatorics
papers.abstract: The 1-2-3 Conjecture asserts that every finite graph without isolated edges admits edge weights from $\{1,2,3\}$ such that the sum function forms a vertex coloring. We study its Borel analogue for locally finite Borel graphs without isolated edges, proving that five weights suffice in general and four suffice for regular graphs. We obtain three weights for acyclic graphs admitting a Borel selection of a nonempty finite set of ends from each component. We also obtain $\mu$-measurable and Baire measurable vertex-coloring $3$-edge weightings from $3$-colorings of the same definability, under probability measure-preserving and Baire quasi-invariance conditions, respectively.

papers.title: On Farah ideals and beyond
papers.abstract: An ideal $\mathcal{I}$ on $\omega$ is called Farah if there are hereditary closed subsets $C_n$ of $\mathcal{P}(\omega)$, for $n\in\omega$, such that $\mathcal{I}=\{A\subseteq\omega:\ \forall_{n\in\omega}\ \exists_{k\in\omega}\ A\setminus k\in C_n\}$. Farah asked in [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 356 (2004), no. 6] if every $\mathbf{F_{\sigma\delta}}$ ideal is a Farah ideal. We show that this is false by providing both tall and non-tall counterexamples. Moreover, we show that there is an antichain in the sense of Kat\v{e}tov order of length $\continuum$ consisting of $\mathbf{F_{\sigma\delta}}$ non-Farah ideals. We also investigate a closely related problem concerning sets of ideal limit points. We show that if $\mathcal{I}$ is an $\mathbf{G_{\delta\sigma\delta}}$ ideal on $\omega$ and $x\in X^\omega$ is a sequence in an uncountable Polish space $X$, then \[ \Lambda_x(\mathcal{I})=\left\{p\in X:\ \exists_{A\notin\mathcal{I}}\ x\restriction A\text{ converges to }p\right\} \] is $\mathbf{F_{\sigma}}$. This answers [Top. App. 312 (2022)] (partially) and [J. Symb. Logic, DOI: 10.1017/jsl.2026.10181]. Earlier it was known to be true only in the case of Farah ideals.

papers.title: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models
papers.abstract: Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.

papers.title: Domain size asymptotics for Markov logic networks
papers.abstract: A Markov logic network (MLN) $\mathbb{M}$ determines a probability distribution $\mathbb{P}_n^\mathbb{M}$ on the set $\mathbf{W}_n$ of structures, or ``possible worlds'', with domain $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. We study the properties of such distributions as $n$ tends to infinity. We show that with mild assumptions on an MLN $\mathbb{M}$ with one soft constraint with an arbitrary positive weight the distribution $\mathbb{P}_n^\mathbb{M}$ will behave quite differently from the uniform distribution $\mathbb{P}_n^{uni}$ on $\mathbf{W}_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For a language with only one relation symbol $R$ which has arity 1 we give an almost complete characterization of the possible asymptotic behaviours of $\mathbb{P}_n^\mathbb{M}$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\mathbb{M}$ may be any MLN for this language. The asymptotic behaviour depends on the soft constraints and weights of the MLN. This characterization is used to show that if the language under consideration contains at least one relation symbol of arity 1 then the following holds: (a) There is an MLN $\mathbb{M}$ such that for every lifted Bayesian network (LBN) $\mathbb{G}$ there are infinitely many $n$ such that $\mathbb{M}$ and $\mathbb{G}$ determine different distributions on $\mathbf{W}_n$. (b) There is an LBN $\mathbb{G}$ such that for every MLN $\mathbb{M}$ there are infinitely many $n$ such that $\mathbb{G}$ and $\mathbb{M}$ determine different distributions on $\mathbf{W}_n$. We also show that, in the limit, the weight dimension and the domain size dimension may behave completely differently.

papers.title: Morita Rigidity for Kleene Algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce Morita equivalence to the study of Kleene algebras and modules. Classical characterizations of Morita-equivalent semirings such as having equivalent categories of modules and one semiring being a full idempotent corner of a finite matrix semiring over the other transfer easily to this new context. We also observe that Morita equivalence can be applied to extending and restricting scalars in Lindenbaum--Tarski algebras of propositional dynamic logics, and that an appropriately-defined category of generalized finite automata satisfies the property that when the underlying Kleene algebras are Morita equivalent then the corresponding categories of generalized automata are equivalent. But the signature results which we obtain relate to rigidity of Kleene algebras in this context. Specifically, every semiring that is Morita-equivalent to the semiring reduct of a Kleene algebra has a unique expansion to a Kleene algebra, and semiring bimodules witnessing Morita-equivalence of semirings which are reducts of Kleene algebras are already Kleene bimodules.

papers.title: A Linear Temporal Logic of Frequencies on Series of Events
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LTLFS, a linear temporal logic for reasoning about frequencies in finite series of probabilistic events. The logic conservatively extends linear temporal logic over finite traces with measure-sensitive operators that compare the empirical distribution observed at any point in a series with an independently specified target distribution. Its semantics integrates the actual sequence of events, the probability distribution governing individual outcomes, and the set of finite assignments compatible with the target frequency. This supports two complementary tasks: verifying whether an observed partial distribution is compatible with the benchmark, and predicting whether and with what probability the completed series can still satisfy it. The language can express observed and attainable frequencies, the probability of realizing a desired final distribution, and conditional probabilities for subsequent outcomes under the assumption that the benchmark is met. We establish formal properties of the operators and characterize their interaction with the temporal structure. A running example concerning representational fairness in sequential outputs from a generative AI system illustrates how the framework can distinguish temporary deviations from irrecoverable violations and support early, logically interpretable intervention. LTLFS thereby provides a symbolic foundation for runtime monitoring of evolving quantitative requirements, with applications to explainable and responsible AI.

papers.title: Polish spaces of separable Banach lattices
papers.abstract: We compare two Polish presentations of separable real Banach lattices: closed sublattices of a universal lattice and closed ideals of $\operatorname{FBL}[\ell_1]$. We construct translations preserving lattice isometry in both directions, continuous and injective from sublattices to ideals and Borel in the reverse direction. Natural generation and Fremlin tensor operations are $\boldsymbol\Sigma^0_2$-measurable with $G_\delta$ graphs. Isometric lattice isomorphism in either universal coding is Borel bireducible with a complete orbit equivalence relation of Polish-group actions. Uniform monotonicity and order uniform smoothness are $\boldsymbol\Pi^0_3$-complete in both codings, whereas strict monotonicity, order smoothness, and order continuity are coanalytic. Abstract $L_p$ and AM-spaces form closed classes of sublattice codes. We also give explicit Borel bounds for atom counts, compact order intervals, and the lattice-isometry classes of $L_p[0,1]$, $\ell_p$, and $c_0$.

papers.title: The model theory of the curve graph
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop a bridge between model theory, geometric topology, and geometric group theory. In particular, we investigate the Ivanov Metaconjecture from the point of view of model theory, and more broadly we seek to answer the general question: why does the curve graph of a surface play such a central role in the study of surfaces and mapping class groups? More specifically, we consider a surface $\Sigma$ of finite type and its curve graph $\mathcal C(\Sigma)$, and we investigate its first-order theory in the language of graph theory. Crucially, $\mathcal C(\Sigma)$ is bi-interpretable with a certain object called the augmented Cayley graph of the mapping class group of the surface. We use this bi-interpretation to prove that the theory of the curve graph is $\omega$--stable, to compute its Morley rank, and to show that it has quantifier elimination with respect to the class of $\forall\exists$--formulae. We also show that many of the complexes which are naturally associated to a surface are interpretable in $\mathcal C(\Sigma)$. This shows that these complexes are all $\omega$--stable and admit certain a priori bounds on their Morley ranks. We are able to use Morley ranks to prove that various complexes are not bi--interpretable with the curve graph. As a consequence of quantifier elimination, we show that algebraic intersection number is not definable in the first order theory of the curve graph. Finally, we prove that the curve graph of a surface enjoys a novel phenomenon that we call interpretation rigidity. That is, if surfaces $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ admits curve graphs that are mutually interpretable, then $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ are homeomorphic to each other. Along the way, numerous technical results are obtained.

papers.title: Decidability and $\neg$NP-completeness for some languages which extend Boolean Set Theory
papers.abstract: We prove the decidability for a class of languages which extend BST and failure of NP-completeness for a subclass of them. The languages BST extended with unordered cartesian product, BST extended with ordered cartesian product and BST extended with powerset fall in this last subclass.

papers.title: Six equations in search of a finite-fold-ness proof
papers.abstract: By following the same construction pattern which Martin Davis proposed in a 1968 paper of his, we have obtained six quaternary quartic Diophantine equations that candidate as `rule-them-all' equations: proving that one of them has only a finite number of integer solutions would suffice to ensure that each recursively enumerable set admits a finite-fold polynomial Diophantine representation.
